risks.description: Political transition uncertainties and economic disruptions following the August 2024 government change could hinder macroeconomic stability and project implementation.
risks.mitigation: Engage across political stakeholders, align project interventions with the National Social Security Strategy (NSSS), and utilize established inter-ministerial steering committees to maintain operational momentum.
risks.evidence: Section I.A, Project Strategic Context: An interim government was sworn in on August 8, 2024, after the former Prime Minister resigned amid a mass uprising.

risks.description: Recurrent extreme weather events like severe flooding and cyclones could damage infrastructure, displace beneficiaries, and disrupt social protection delivery systems.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize climate-vulnerable locations, house MIS platforms in National Data Centers with disaster recovery centers, and utilize the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) if emergency funds are needed.
risks.evidence: Section I.A, Project Strategic Context: Recurring flooding affects a greater share of the population than any other natural hazard, affecting more than 1 million people annually.

risks.description: High inflation rates could erode the real purchasing power of cash transfer allowance benefits, reducing the overall welfare impact on poor households.
risks.mitigation: Establish and implement a standardized benefit adequacy framework to periodically review and index cash transfer benefit levels against poverty lines and consumption baskets.
risks.evidence: Section I.B, Sectoral Context: Inflation remained elevated, reaching 9.9 percent in January 2025... real value of benefits under DSS allowance programs has decreased.

risks.description: High targeting error rates (inclusion and exclusion errors) in safety net selection could prevent assistance from reaching the poorest eligible populations.
risks.mitigation: Establish and roll out a Dynamic Social Registry (DSR) utilizing objective Proxy Means Testing (PMT) and authenticated NID/BRN verification for beneficiary targeting.
risks.evidence: Section I.B, Sectoral Context: Nearly half (47 percent) of the poor households are not covered by any social assistance program.

risks.description: Lack of inter-institutional coordination and missing inter-ministerial mandates could derail integration and data sharing across line ministries for the Dynamic Social Registry.
risks.mitigation: Institutionalize a DSR Steering Committee under Cabinet Division, establish a DSR Coordination Committee at Finance Division, and execute binding MoUs among participating ministries.
risks.evidence: Section I.B, Sectoral Context: Past efforts to create a social registry... did not materialize due to... lack of institutional mandate to drive integration.

risks.description: Financial management complexity across multiple implementing agencies, varied grant mechanisms, and cash transfers could cause accounting delays or non-compliance.
risks.mitigation: Deploy certified FM consultants at PIUs, mainstream the iBAS++ system with distinct ministry budget codes, conduct annual independent internal audits, and enforce POM procedures.
risks.evidence: Section IV.B, Fiduciary: From the FM perspective, the project design is complex due to the intricacy of activity selection and various IAs and finances.

risks.description: Delays in establishing required PIUs, approving the Project Operations Manual (POM), and setting up steering committees within statutory deadlines could delay implementation.
risks.mitigation: Establish close tracking of legal covenant milestones, draw experienced fiduciary personnel from previous World Bank projects, and finalize the POM early.
risks.evidence: Datasheet, Legal Covenants: The Recipient shall establish within six (6) months of the Effective Date... the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the DSS.

risks.description: Digital literacy gaps, social norms, and mobility constraints among vulnerable women, PWDs, and elderly could limit their access to DSR registration and G2P payments.
risks.mitigation: Design accessible offline/online interfaces with audio support, establish localized Upazila registration access points, and train field social workers for targeted outreach.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, Component 1: The activity plans will ensure the DSR, and associated platforms are user-friendly for women with limited literacy or digital skills.

risks.description: Data security and privacy vulnerabilities in the Dynamic Social Registry platform could expose personal beneficiary socioeconomic information to unauthorized access.
risks.mitigation: Enforce national data security regulations, integrate strict data protection guidelines into the POM, and host data inside National Data Centers with disaster recovery protocols.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, Component 1: GoB will adhere to its national data security regulations; the design of the DSR... will contain clear mitigation measures.

risks.description: Ad-hoc skills training, lack of savings mechanisms, and weak market linkages in existing livelihoods programs could hinder participants' long-term graduation out of poverty.
risks.mitigation: Deliver bundled economic inclusion services including revised market-aligned training, financial literacy, training stipends, productive grants, mentorship, and market connections.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, Component 3: evaluation reports no long-term impact on household savings and asset creation and limited participation (7 percent) in skill enhancement trainings.

risks.description: Failure or delays in meeting specific Performance-Based Condition (PBC) targets could lead to delayed IDA disbursements and counterpart cash flow shortfalls.
risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated tracking of PBC indicators, provide capacity building for frontline cadres, and maintain accurate reporting of eligible cash transfer expenditures under code 3721.
risks.evidence: Section III.C, Disbursement Arrangements: Financing earmarked for PBCs would be disbursed... upon fulfilment of conditions/achievement of results outlined in the Results Framework.

risks.description: Shortfalls or delays in procuring substantial government counterpart funding (US$3,848M) could restrict safety net financing and cash transfer distributions.
risks.mitigation: Monitor legal covenants regarding counterpart obligations and ensure required safety net allocations are prioritized in annual government budget submissions through Finance Division.
risks.evidence: Datasheet, Summary Financing Data: Counterpart Funding Borrower/Recipient US$ 3,848.00 million.

risks.description: Fiduciary risks and accounting delays associated with sub-grants transferred directly to community social clubs could lead to improper fund utilization.
risks.mitigation: Enforce strict registration and due diligence requirements for clubs, mandate separate bank accounts with joint signatories, and require monthly countersigned SOE reporting.
risks.evidence: Section IV.B, Financial Management: Grants to social clubs... will be financed through the DSS’s DA... Club’s SOE must be countersigned by a designated DSS representative.

risks.description: Unforeseen eligible crises triggering the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) could divert financial and administrative resources away from core project activities.
risks.mitigation: Prepare and adopt a CERC Manual and Emergency Action Plan early to ensure streamlined emergency protocols without compromising core project management structures.
risks.evidence: Datasheet, Conditions: Adopting CERC Manual and Emergency Action Plan... in respect of Emergency Expenditures under Category (7).
